The transient launch request carries only the approved session code-workspace root, the loopback MCP endpoint, the selected requirement, and a direct-network policy projection derived from the existing `NetworkAccess` capability. It is not serialized. `ExternalAssetAcquisition` remains a governed GameEngine/MCP capability and therefore does not silently widen ambient child-process network access. The persisted run/audit record contains only the non-secret confinement profile and its truthful guarantee levels. MCP authorization material remains process-environment-only.

The launch boundary exposes a confinement-provider seam so first-class adapters or platform integrations can own the real process creation mechanism. A profile satisfies the strict requirement only when it reports provider, OS, container, or VM confinement with enforced filesystem, network, and process-tree guarantees. Unsupported generic launches report unavailable rather than simulated confinement.
new:
The transient launch request carries only the approved session code-workspace root, the loopback MCP endpoint, the selected requirement, and a direct-network policy projection derived from the existing `NetworkAccess` capability. It is not serialized. `ExternalAssetAcquisition` remains a governed GameEngine/MCP capability and therefore does not silently widen ambient child-process network access. The persisted run/audit record contains only the non-secret confinement profile and its truthful guarantee levels. The generic application-policy-only launcher retains the existing MCP token delivery for compatibility and therefore explicitly reports credential secrecy as unavailable; it can never satisfy the strict confinement requirement.

The launch boundary exposes a confinement-provider seam so first-class adapters or platform integrations can own the real process creation mechanism. A profile satisfies the strict requirement only when it reports provider, OS, container, or VM confinement with enforced filesystem, network, process-tree, **and credential-secrecy** guarantees. A provider reporting credential secrecy as enforced must keep provider credentials, MCP authorization material, and inherited credential-bearing parent environment out of the sandboxed child, using a provider-native broker/helper or equivalent protected channel when credentials are required. Unsupported generic launches report unavailable rather than simulated confinement.
